summary: Static verification of E1's (1) Clear-Saved-Data-On-Logout and (2) Pull-To-Refresh-Feedback features across /app/PartnerApp (==/app/frontend) and /app/Customer. Scope reviewed: both RefreshNote.tsx (identical files), both AuthContext.tsx logout paths, frontend/src/lib/queryPersist.ts clearSavedHomeData, both root _layout.tsx (provider ordering + RefreshNoteHost mount), CustomerShell.tsx pull-to-refresh wiring, Customer/app/(site)/index.tsx wrapper usage, CustomerDataContext.tsx post-logout cache safety, and all 28 PartnerApp files that had their RefreshControl import rewritten. Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` on PartnerApp (24 pre-existing errors, none in touched files or related to the import rewrites), `npx eslint` on touched files (0 errors, 9 benign Animated.Value `.interpolate` ref-in-render warnings — standard RN Animated pattern, not real bugs), and a careful logic review for double-notify, timer leaks, children-prop preservation, and post-logout cache rewrites. Customer app has no node_modules so tsc not run there — but all touched Customer files are syntactically valid (verified by eslint parse via scoping and manual review); logic mirrors PartnerApp exactly for RefreshNote.

static_review_findings.frontend/src/components/RefreshNote.tsx: Identical. Wrapper correctly spreads {...props} to RNRefreshControl so Android ScrollView's refreshControl children-clone keeps all children + original props (tintColor, colors, progressBackgroundColor, etc.). onRefresh is overridden by `handle` which (a) marks pulled, (b) sets a 1200ms fallback setTimeout for screens that never flip `refreshing`, (c) if onRefresh returns a Promise, hooks .finally to call done() ONLY if sawSpin is still false — i.e. only when the screen never used the `refreshing` prop. done() is idempotent via `pulled.current` guard: once called, pulled flips to false and subsequent paths early-return → no double-notify. useEffect([refreshing]) correctly flips sawSpin on true, calls done() on true→false, and clears the fallback timer when the real spin starts. Cleanup effect clears the timer on unmount. RefreshNoteHost subscribes a single fn to the module-level `subs` Set; animates in via spring, auto-hides after 1800ms, cleans up its own setTimeout + subs.delete on unmount. testID='refresh-updated-note' present. Pill is pointerEvents='none' so it never blocks touches.
static_review_findings.frontend/src/context/AuthContext.tsx log: Uses useQueryClient() → valid because AuthProvider is nested inside QueryClientProvider in app/_layout.tsx (QueryClientProvider → ErrorBoundary → ThemedRoot → ThemeProvider → BrandProvider → AuthProvider). Order of ops in logout: setToken(null) → setUser(null) → clearSavedHomeData() → qc.clear(). Order is safe — clearing token first ensures any in-flight queries that re-run won't resave fresh data (they'd fail 401), and qc.clear() last ensures no React-Query re-subscriber grabs stale data. Partner has no in-provider persistent-data debounced writer like Customer, so no race.
static_review_findings.Customer/src/context/AuthContext.tsx log: Mirrors Partner but inlines the AsyncStorage sweep with prefix 'cust_home_cache_v1_'. AuthProvider is correctly nested inside QueryClientProvider in Customer/app/_layout.tsx. qc.clear() called last.
static_review_findings.frontend/src/lib/queryPersist.ts clearSa: AsyncStorage.getAllKeys().filter(k => k.startsWith('partner_home_cache_v1_')) → multiRemove. Wrapped in try/catch (ignored). Clears every account's partner snapshot — same as Customer side. Note: this is intentional multi-account wipe; aligns with the 'shared phones stay private' requirement.
static_review_findings.Customer/src/context/CustomerDataContext: cacheKey = user?.id ? `cust_home_cache_v1_${user.id}` : ''. The debounced save effect at line 127-133 early-returns on `!cacheKey`, so once user becomes null the next effect re-run skips the storage.setItem. The in-flight 1000ms timer from the previous render is cleared by the effect's cleanup. One micro-race: if the 1000ms setTimeout already fired BEFORE user flipped to null (i.e. the write is already queued on the JS event loop), the write still happens — but logout runs AFTER user is set to null and only THEN calls clearSavedHomeData/qc.clear… wait, Customer's logout order is: setToken(null) → setUser(null) → sweep AsyncStorage → qc.clear(). Because setUser is synchronous but the sweep is async, there's a tiny theoretical window where a previously-queued save setTimeout could rewrite the key AFTER the sweep. Rated: VERY LOW risk — the save is debounced 1000ms and the sweep runs within microseconds of setUser(null); a save fired right before setUser(null) completes before the sweep awaits. Not a user-visible bug. Suggestion (nit, optional): await a microtask tick before multiRemove, or run multiRemove AFTER qc.clear() and setBookings([]) — but current ordering is acceptable for this feature.
static_review_findings.frontend/app/_layout.tsx: RefreshNoteHost mounted once inside ToastProvider → above the Stack, inside SafeAreaProvider (useSafeAreaInsets works). Provider stack: Query → ErrorBoundary → Theme → Brand → Auth → Realtime → Chat → Toast → Stack + RefreshNoteHost. ✓
static_review_findings.Customer/app/_layout.tsx: RefreshNoteHost mounted once inside ToastProvider, after the Stack, inside SafeAreaProvider. Provider stack: Query → ErrorBoundary → Theme → Brand → Auth → Cart → Realtime → Toast → Stack + RefreshNoteHost. ✓
static_review_findings.Customer/src/components/customer/Custome: Imports RefreshControl from react-native directly (intentional — not the wrapper) and manually calls notifyRefreshed() after `await runPullRefresh()`. This bypasses the auto-detection and works because runPullRefresh is awaited before clearing `pulling`. Correct.
static_review_findings.Customer/app/(site)/index.tsx: Imports RefreshControl from '@/src/components/RefreshNote' and uses it on the FlatList's refreshControl prop with refreshing={refreshing} + onRefresh={() => refetch()}. The wrapper will auto-notify once the pull completes. ✓

No file broke its react-native imports.

eslint_results: Touched PartnerApp files: 0 errors, 9 warnings. All 9 warnings are react-hooks/refs false-positives on the Animated.Value `a` being passed to `a.interpolate()` inside style — this is the standard React Native Animated API pattern and is not a bug.
critical_code_review_comments: Nit (very low risk): Customer logout order is setToken→setUser→multiRemove→qc.clear(). CustomerDataContext's debounced 1s save setTimeout, if already queued when setUser flips, could theoretically fire AFTER multiRemove and rewrite the just-cleared cust_home_cache_v1_<uid> key. The window is a sub-millisecond gap between the setUser synchronous update and the next microtask that awaits getAllKeys. In practice the chance of a save-timer firing in exactly that gap is negligible, but if E1 wants belt-and-suspenders, call qc.clear() + AsyncStorage sweep BEFORE setUser(null) is NOT safe either (would cause mid-logout 401 state leakage); better fix is: in CustomerDataContext save effect, also gate on `user?.id` (not just cacheKey) and clear in-memory bookings/wallet/refunds state when user becomes null — then even a late timer writes an empty snapshot that would be overwritten on next login's fresh hydrate. Current behaviour is already acceptable for the user-visible requirement (shared-phone privacy).

Nit: clearSavedHomeData() wipes partner_home_cache_v1_* for ALL accounts, not just the logging-out user. Intentional per requirement but worth noting — if two partner users share a device and one logs out, the other's cached home snapshot is also removed. Acceptable; the UX trade-off is explicit in the requirement wording.

Nit: RefreshNote.tsx cleanup effect `useEffect(() => () => { if (timer.current) clearTimeout(timer.current); }, [])` disables lint but doesn't clear the timer when the RefreshControl prop changes identity on each render — fine because timer.current is a ref not a state.
Nit: notifyRefreshed() is module-global. If two different RefreshNoteHosts are ever mounted (e.g. by hot-reload), both will animate. Current _layout.tsx mounts exactly one, so OK.
